newsitem.title: USA: Conseco upgraded to buy by Dean Witter.
newsitem.headline: Conseco upgraded to buy by Dean Witter.

text.p: Dean Witter analyst Michael Lewis said he upgraded Conseco Inc to buy from accumulate on optimism about the company's acquisition moves.
Lewis said he raised his 1997 earnings estimate to $5 a share from $4.65 and raised his price target for the shares to $52 from $47.
"We view these acquisitions as being distinctly positive," Lewis said, improving Conseco's mix of business and providing increased earnings stability.
The deals also enable Conseco to "solidify their position in some of their key market places," he said.
The deals will make Conseco the largest writer of long-term care insurance and the second largest in cancer insurance, he said. It also will bolster Conseco's position in the annuity market, he said.
Conseco, based in Carmel, Ind., is known for its Medicare supplement, long-term care, annuity and traditional life insurance products.

It said today it had agreed to buy Capitol American Financial Corp and American Travellers Corp. In addition, it agreed to acquire the shares it does not already own of American Life Holdings and Bankers Life Holding Corp.
Lewis said he was not concerned that Conseco was taking on more than it could handle with so many deals.
"They have been an important factor in the consolidation of the insurance industry for years," he said. "They have the teams in place and the systems to continue to make consolidating acquisitions."
The acquisitions will be a challenge, he said, but added, "I think they will be able to handle it without missing a beat."
